setup.createSub: Make your admin account. This is the main character of the server — pick a name and a strong password.
setup.tokenWhy: You're not on the server's home network, so prove it's yours: grab the one-time setup token from the server's screen (the console login shows it) or its log (journalctl -u nocapos).
setup.tokenMissing: Pop in the setup token first — it's on the server's screen or in its log.
setup.nameRule: Names are 3–32 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
setup.passwordShort: Too short — use at least 10 characters.
setup.passwordMismatch: Those passwords don't match. Try again?
setup.localHint: You're on the server's own network, so no token needed. No cap.
wiz.title: Set up NoCapOS
wiz.step.name: Name
wiz.introSub: You're in, {name}. A few quick steps to make this server yours — skip anything, it's all in Settings later.
wiz.voiceText: How should NoCapOS talk to you? You can switch any time in Settings.
wiz.voiceSample: Bet — your files are synced. No cap.
wiz.lookText: Everything applies right away, so you see it live.
wiz.modeHint: Light and Auto use the NoCap classic theme; Glass and Cyber-Deck stay dark.
wiz.nameText: This is how it shows up on your network.
wiz.hostLen: Give it a name of 1 to 63 characters.
wiz.hostChars: Only letters, digits and dashes (not at the start or end), e.g. living-room-nas.
wiz.hostDigits: The name can't be only digits.
wiz.nativeOnly: This one needs NoCapOS installed straight on Linux. Skip it for now.
wiz.netText: Let your router hand out the address (DHCP), or pin a static one.
wiz.netNone: No adapter NoCapOS can change here. Skip it.
wiz.netUnsupported: Changing the network needs NoCapOS on Linux with NetworkManager. Skip it.
wiz.netSafe: Safety net: if this browser can't reach the server on its new address within a minute, the old settings come back by themselves.
wiz.netBadV4: Enter the IPv4 address with its prefix, e.g. 192.168.1.50/24.
wiz.netBadGw4: The IPv4 gateway looks off, e.g. 192.168.1.1.
wiz.netBadDns4: IPv4 DNS servers look like 1.1.1.1, separated by commas.
wiz.netBadV6: Enter the IPv6 address with its prefix, e.g. fd00::50/64.
wiz.netBadGw6: The IPv6 gateway looks off, e.g. fe80::1.
wiz.netBadDns6: IPv6 DNS servers look like fd00::1, separated by commas.
wiz.timeText: So schedules, backups and logs run on your time.
wiz.desktop: NoCap Desktop on the server's screen
wiz.desktopHint: Plug in a monitor and use the server like a full computer.
wiz.updatesHint: See if there's a fresher NoCapOS right now.
wiz.sumText: Looks good? Tap Apply. Anything you skipped stays exactly how it is.
wiz.updateAvail: {v} is out — update from Glow Up
wiz.updateNone: You're on the latest. No cap.
wiz.netReverted: The new address didn't answer, so the old network settings are back.
wiz.netOpenNew: Switching… open the new address to keep it:
wiz.netChecking: Switching… checking we can still reach the server.
wiz.netConfirming: Locking in the new network settings…
wiz.netKept: New network settings locked in. Bet.
wiz.doneText: Your server, your rules. Open The Roster from the dock to find every app, or press Ctrl+Space to search anything.
